common_name: Lanarth White Hydrangea (Classic Pure White Lacecap Hydrangea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Lanarth White is a classic pure white lacecap hydrangea, an RHS Award of Garden Merit winner.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade. Lanarth White bears crisp, pure white lacecap blooms, a flat outer ring of showy sterile florets surrounding a central disk of small fertile flowers, unaffected by soil pH the way blue and pink cultivars are since white pigments don't shift with aluminum availability. Its clean, classic lacecap form and reliable performance have earned it a Royal Horticultural Society Award of Garden Merit. It blooms on old wood, so prune only immediately after flowering to shape, and give it morning sun with afternoon shade in hot climates to prevent wilting.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Veitchii is an older lacecap hydrangea whose white sterile florets age to soft pink or blue.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade. Veitchii bears lacecap blooms that open crisp white and gradually age to soft pink or blue depending on soil pH, giving the flower head a two-toned effect as older and newer florets sit side by side, unlike white cultivars whose color never shifts. It has been in cultivation since the 19th century and remains valued for its refined lacecap form. It blooms on old wood, so prune only immediately after flowering, and give it morning sun with afternoon shade in hot climates to prevent wilting.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Zorro is grown as much for its near-black stems as for its color-shifting mophead blooms.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade. Zorro bears striking near-black stems that contrast dramatically with its rounded mophead blooms, which shift blue in acidic soil and pink in alkaline soil like other Hydrangea macrophylla cultivars; amend with aluminum sulfate to intensify blue tones in the alkaline soils common across the Gulf South. The dark stems provide ornamental interest year-round, even in winter after the leaves drop. It blooms on old wood, so prune only immediately after flowering, and give it morning sun with afternoon shade in hot climates to prevent wilting.

common_name: Merritt's Supreme Hydrangea (Deep Red-Pink to Blue Mophead)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Merritt's Supreme is a vigorous older mophead cultivar known for exceptionally deep color.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade. Merritt's Supreme bears large, rounded mophead blooms in deep red-pink in alkaline soil, shifting to a rich, saturated blue in acidic soil, among the more intensely colored older mophead cultivars still in commerce. Its vigorous, reliable growth and dependable, long-lasting blooms have kept it popular for decades. It blooms on old wood, so prune only immediately after flowering, and give it morning sun with afternoon shade in hot Southern climates to prevent wilting.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Kardinal is a bright red mophead cultivar bred primarily for the cut-flower trade.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade. Kardinal bears vivid, bright red mophead blooms, a color that resists shifting toward purple or blue even in acidic soil more strongly than many other red or pink hydrangea cultivars, making it a favorite for florists needing a dependable, true red. Its sturdy stems and long vase life suit it especially well for cutting. It blooms on old wood, so prune only immediately after flowering, and give it morning sun with afternoon shade in hot climates to prevent wilting.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Masja is a compact mophead cultivar bearing deep pink-red blooms.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade. Masja bears compact, rounded mophead blooms in deep pink-red on a smaller, more manageable shrub than many mophead cultivars, fitting foundation plantings and containers where full-size hydrangea would need frequent pruning to control. Its compact habit and reliable, saturated color have made it a popular choice for smaller gardens. It blooms on old wood, so prune only immediately after flowering, and give it morning sun with afternoon shade in hot climates to prevent wilting.
